title: Question about a couple of things in "The Substance 2024"

commenti.body:
The biker crashing into the screen is immediately followed with her waking up suddenly, the implication there is that this is a dream she was having. Iirc she wakes up in intense pain due to her misuse of the substance, so 1. The bike crashing into her puts us in her headspace of what she must feel like in this moment, aka, just got hit by a motorcycle. Also, she wakes up into her old body I think, which makes her new biker boyfriend unattainable for the time being, so he’s all wrapped up in her own self loathing and represents the things she can no longer have when she’s in her old body. So it makes sense that in the dream, he is the thing crashing into her. She figures (correctly) that he is disgusted by her old form

As far as the abstract lights go, I saw these are representations of what she’s seeing in her head while she’s in immense pain caused by the substance, or some kind of hallucination brought on by the splitting process. I don’t think it symbolizes something directly, I think it’s more about communicating visually the experience of putting yourself through this process. It’s so painful that it makes you see bright lights, or, the process of your brain splitting in half and duplicating comes along with some visual hallucinations. More of a tonal flourish than some kind of direct symbol

The abstract visuals we see when she's splitting are, at least in part, a reference to the star gate sequence in 2001: A Space Odyssey. 

It symbolizes both the crossing of a new evolutionary frontier and some kind of transcendental "youth" as seen from Elizabeth's POV at that early stage in the story, although Fargeat undercuts that later with reference to The Shining: we're shown the ugly and misleading side of this transformation with echoes of that decaying crone that tempts Jack in the bathroom.

The biker and the chicken leg in the body nightmares are there to show that even while asleep Elisabeth and Sue have some awareness of what the other is doing. It’s important because it shows they really do share a subconscious to some degree, even if they are separate.

And then, as others said, the visuals during the transition are a bit more abstract about consciousness passing between bodies and this idea that a new heart has ignited. 

[If you want a literary analysis of The Substance](https://filmcolossus.com/the-substance-explained-2024)

I found the guy's personality and lack of depth to be so abhorrent and unattractive that I failed to consider her perspective (I know he 'likes me' but he won't like me like this) when she returned to her original body. So his screaming at her and speeding away will likely have a bit more impact on rewatch, thanks!
